datasets.name: UAV tilt photography imagery
datasets.verbatim: In this study, the approach to close waypoint planning is to first use a larger altitude to carry out a larger range of orthophoto aerial photography and establish a coarse model. On the rough model, the disaster areas that need to be finely modeled are selected for low altitude tilt photography route planning.

datasets.name: Ground penetrating radar (GPR) scanning data
datasets.verbatim: To verify the above inference, ground penetrating radar (GPR) scanning was conducted on the filled area on July 16th.

methods.name: UAV-based tilt photography, 3D reconstruction, and spatial analysis
methods.summary: The method involves planning UAV flight paths for tilt photography, performing multi-view geometry-based 3D reconstruction (photo alignment, depth map construction, mesh reconstruction, and texture reconstruction), and conducting grid-based spatial analysis to compare multi-temporal 3D models for landslide evolution and volume estimation.

availability.author_statement: The data presented in this study are available upon request from the corresponding author.

reproducibility_assessment: The landslide inventory and other input datasets are not referenced or linked, and the custom code used for 3D reconstruction and spatial analysis is not provided.
